items.title: 'Bathtub ring' on Mars offers best evidence yet of ancient ocean

featured_image.name: "Bathtub Ring" is New Evidence for an Ancient Ocean on Mars

items.description:
A vast ocean may have once lapped against the shores of Mars for millions of years, according to a study published Wednesday in the journal Nature that identifies a geological formation on the Red Planet strikingly similar to the continental shelves found along Earth's coastlines.[1][2]

Researchers Abdallah Zaki, a postdoctoral scholar at the University of Texas at Austin, and Michael Lamb, a professor of geology at Caltech, found a wide, flat band of terrain wrapping the boundary between Mars's northern lowlands and southern highlands — a feature they liken to the ring left around a drained bathtub. The ocean it implies would have covered roughly a third of the planet's surface.[3][1]

items.title: Brazil's ex-spy chief freed from ICE custody in US

featured_image.name: Former Brazil spy chief freed in the US after ICE detention ...

items.description:
Former Brazilian intelligence chief Alexandre Ramagem was released from U.S. immigration custody on Wednesday, just two days after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Orlando, Florida, according to Reuters. His release was announced by Bolsonaro ally Paulo Figueiredo on the social media platform X, writing "Alexandre Ramagem is free," while Ramagem's name was also removed from ICE's online detainee database.[1]

ICE did not respond to inquiries about the release, and Reuters reported it was unable to determine Ramagem's current immigration status in the United States.[1]

items.title: US insists Lebanon, Iran peace talks stay on separate tracks

featured_image.name: Senate Republicans again reject resolution to rein in Trump's Iran war

items.description:
The Trump administration has made clear that any peace deal between Israel and Lebanon must be negotiated independently of the ongoing U.S.-Iran nuclear talks, a deliberate decoupling designed to deny Tehran leverage over the pace of diplomacy on either front.

A senior U.S. official told Axios that Washington has not asked Israel for a ceasefire in Lebanon, and that the Lebanon track is not part of the peace negotiations with Iran. The official added that President Donald Trump would "welcome and be happy with an end of hostilities" as part of an agreement reached directly between Israel and Lebanon.[1][2]

items.title: Israel's security cabinet to weigh Lebanon ceasefire

featured_image.name: Israel said to agree in principle to Lebanon ceasefire offer ...

items.description:
Israel's security cabinet is set to convene Wednesday evening to discuss a possible ceasefire in Lebanon, according to a senior Israeli official who spoke to Reuters, a development that follows the first direct diplomatic engagement between Israel and Lebanon in more than three decades.[1][2]

The cabinet meeting, scheduled for 8 p.m. local time, comes one day after Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors met at the U.S. State Department in Washington for over two hours of talks hosted by Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The trilateral meeting — which included Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter and Lebanese Ambassador Nada Hamadeh Moawad — concluded with all sides agreeing to "launch direct negotiations at a mutually agreed time and venue," according to a State Department statement.[3][4][5]

items.title: CENTCOM says Iran naval blockade 'fully implemented' after 48 hours

featured_image.name: U.S. Centcom says blockade of Iranian ports begins Monday

items.description:
The U.S. military said Wednesday that ten vessels had complied with orders to turn around and return toward Iranian ports or coastal areas during the first 48 hours of a naval blockade, as Washington moved to choke off Tehran's maritime trade amid the ongoing war.[1][2][3]

"No vessels have made it past US forces," U.S. Central Command said in a statement posted on X, declaring the blockade "fully implemented" after just 36 hours. CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper said U.S. forces had "completely halted economic trade going in and out of Iran by sea," noting that roughly 90 percent of Iran's economy depends on international maritime commerce.[4][5][6]

items.title: Chinese tanker turned back at Hormuz as US blockade holds

featured_image.name: First Tanker Makes It Out of Hormuz Amid US Blockade and It's a ...

items.description: A U.S.-sanctioned Chinese-owned tanker that appeared to defy President Trump's naval blockade of Iranian ports has turned back toward the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, according to Reuters, underscoring how the three-day-old blockade is rapidly becoming a flashpoint in U.S.-China relations. The incident involving the Rich Starry — a Malawi-flagged vessel owned by Shanghai Xuanrun Shipping — has stoked fears that any direct American interception of a Chinese-linked ship could trigger a diplomatic crisis weeks before a planned Trump-Xi summit in Beijing.[1][2]
